note: Built-in hijack rules, consumed by tools/bncm_preload.js at document start.
Two rule types:
replace     -- match a module FACTORY by a source fragment and rewrite the text with
new Function().  This reproduces upstream BetterNCM's manifest `hijacks`
semantics (upstream rewrote the response body of orpheus://orpheus/pub/<x>
from inside the client, which needs a CEF scheme handler; see
docs/06-plugin-framework.md section 7).
wrap-export -- match a module by a source fragment, then replace the EXPORTED function the
moment the module executes.  Nicer when it works, because it does not depend
on the minifier keeping local names spelled the same way -- BUT it cannot
work for webpack harmony exports in this bundle: the runtime helper is
`r.d = function(e,c,d){ r.o(e,c) || Object.defineProperty(e,c,{enumerable:!0,
get:d}) }` with `configurable` left at its default of false, so the binding
is not replaceable from outside.  The engine reports that loudly instead of
pretending to have hooked anything.
Every rule records the frontend pack it was derived from.  Because web.pack updates
independently of the client, a rule that matches nothing is REPORTED (window.__BNCM_HIJACK__
.missed, and the plugin manager's 诊断 tab) rather than silently ignored.  Re-derive with
tools/hijack_probe.mjs when that happens.
How a pack update is actually handled here: re-verification runs OFFLINE against the installed
web.pack -- exactly what the drift guard in test/preload-engine.test.mjs does, reading the
container from disk.  tools/hijack_probe.mjs is NOT used for this, because it needs
window.__BNCM_WP__, which only exists once the preload's webpack interposition is on -- and that
interposition alone stops the client from mounting (see the two rules below and docs/11 section
7/8).  Treat the probe as a deliberate experiment: temporarily enable a rule, on a throwaway
session, and expect a blank window.

rules.unsafe_reason: OFF BY DEFAULT: enabling this blanked the client too. See the note in why[].
why: RefinedNowPlaying defines window.onProcessLyrics and publishes window.currentLyrics,
dispatching `lyrics-updated` for consumers such as LyricBar.  The hook has no caller of its
own: the caller is the client's lyric pipeline, so without this rule nothing arrives.
Upstream made that caller exist by rewriting orpheus://orpheus/pub/core with a byte-exact
fragment of the 2.10.4-era minified code.  That resource no longer exists in 3.1.41 and the
fragment matches nothing, so the target was re-derived.  In 3.1.41 the pipeline entry point is:
n.d(t,"a",(function(){return a}));
function a(e){const t={currentUsedLyric:"none",currentUsedLyricVersion:-1,...};
if(!e.lrc&&!e.yrc)return t; let n=[],i=[];if(e.lrc){...} if(e.yrc){...} }
which converts the raw lyric API payload (lrc / yrc / tlyric / romalrc / ytlrc / yromalrc)
into the display model.  The `from` fragment sits after the model is initialised and before
any lyric field is read, so the payload can reach the hook before the client parses it.
Re-verified against web.pack 83304b1 (the build now installed): still exactly one occurrence
in app.chunk and one in subApp.chunk (the same module is duplicated across two bundles),
and none elsewhere.
Why `replace` and not `wrap-export`: the export binding is a non-configurable accessor (see
the file note), so the export cannot be swapped.  Rewriting the factory text before it is
registered sidesteps that entirely.
The injected code calls the hook for its side effects and passes the payload through when
one comes back.  RNP kicks processing off in a setTimeout and ends with `return Ge(e,t)`,
so the return value is normally a no-op and must NOT be awaited.  A throwing hook is
swallowed and logged so a plugin cannot break the client's own lyric path.
*** WHY IT IS NOW DISABLED (pending: true) ***
On the live client this rule DID apply (applied: ["builtin:lyrics-hook", ...]) and the
client went blank: #root 0 children, the app's content containers gone, and the page-error
tripwire recorded three `Script error.` events at the same moment.  A control run with every
plugin loaded but no rewrite active rendered normally.
The cause is structural and shared with builtin:redux-dispatch-hook: a rewritten factory is
rebuilt with `new Function('return (' + source + ')')()`, which RECREATES the function in
global scope and DROPS ITS ORIGINAL CLOSURE.  Any module that resolves even one free
identifier from the enclosing webpack/vendor scope throws at run time, and one throwing
module aborts the boot.  Being careful about which fragment to pick is not enough -- the
mechanism itself is the problem.
The real fix is a SCOPE-PRESERVING rewrite; see docs/11 section 7 for the two candidates
(re-enter the module through its own factory via a Proxy, or evaluate the patched source in
the module's own scope by reusing its arguments object).  Both need live validation, and the
page-error tripwire in this preload is what makes that safe to attempt.

rules.unsafe_reason: OFF BY DEFAULT: enabling this blanked the client. See the note below.
why: This is RefinedNowPlayingNext's OWN 3.1.11+ mechanism, taken verbatim from its manifest: it
exposes window.rnpDispatchHook so the plugin can observe redux actions (song changes, play
state) without depending on the 2.x DOM or on the lyric-pipeline hijack.
Upstream expresses it as a response-body rewrite of orpheus://orpheus/pub/hybrid/vendors.
The loader applies the same fragment at module-factory level instead.  Re-verified against
web.pack 83304b1 (the build now installed): the fragment still occurs exactly once, in
vendors~app~subApp.chunk.  On the live client (measured against 477f8a2) the engine really
did rewrite that module (module 1979,
modulesRewritten=1, window.rnpDispatchHook became defined).
*** WHY IT IS DISABLED (pending: true) ***
Enabling it leaves the app UI unmounted: measured, #root had 0 children and the app's
container had height 0, while a control run with every plugin loaded but NO hijack rewrote
anything and rendered normally (rootKids=2, bodyTextLen=2100).  The cause is structural: a
rewritten factory is produced by `new Function('return (' + source + ')')()`, which RECREATES
the function in global scope and therefore DROPS THE ORIGINAL CLOSURE.  Any module that
resolves a free identifier from its enclosing webpack/vendor scope throws at run time, and
one throwing module is enough to abort the app's boot.
Do not flip this to false without first proving the target module has no free variables
outside (module, exports, __webpack_require__) -- and re-run test\autostart.cmd plus a visual
check afterwards.  A scope-preserving rewrite is the real fix and is tracked in docs/11 §7.
Until then RNP-Next still loads and still publishes window.rnpDispatchHook; only the
dispatch feed is missing, so it falls back to the lyrics-pipeline data path.
